title: Your first setup checklist
intro: Set the foundations before you invite the whole team. A short, controlled start makes the first working week easier.
blocks: Confirm your access. Use the Business Owner account supplied for your business. Check that the business name is yours and that you can see Business and Payroll. A standard Manager account has different access.

Check the package. Confirm Clockx or Full Workspace, the employee allowance and any enabled add-ons. Ask DayRidge to correct the account configuration before building a workflow around a missing feature.
Set the business basics. Review your business details, pay frequency, payday rule, weekly labour budget and automatic unpaid-break rule. Save, then check the calculated pay-period preview.
Add a small pilot team. Check names, employee numbers, working patterns, start dates and access emails. Add your Managers separately from employee shift profiles.
Run one complete shift. Publish a shift, confirm the employee can see it, record clock-in and clock-out, review breaks and check the resulting worked hours.
Roll out to the rest of the team. Explain who handles questions, when rotas are published and how leave and corrections should be requested.
One employee can sign in, see a published shift, record attendance and find their hours. You can review that record from the owner workspace.

title: The DayRidge values
intro: Four promises guide how we explain, build and improve DayRidge. They should be visible in the experience of using it, not just in the brochure.
blocks: Clear pricing, honest answers and no unnecessary jargon. We explain what each package includes, which tools cost extra and where the product has limits. If something needs a conversation, we say so.
Practical tools for busy businesses. Plan the rota, record the hours and handle the everyday requests that come with running a team. Good software should reduce friction in real work.
Clear responsibilities, sensible permissions and care with personal information. Employees get information relevant to them; owners control access to more sensitive business and employee records.
Listen to businesses, challenge unnecessary admin and keep improving the product. We focus innovation on useful changes that help owners, managers and employees work more clearly.
What this means for your business
You should be able to understand the tools, the price and the next step. Ask for a clear explanation whenever a setting, feature or package is unclear.

title: Know what your account includes
intro: A package provides tools. A role provides access. Optional add-ons provide extra workflows only when they are enabled for the business.
blocks: Rota, clocking, recorded payroll hours and annual leave
Sickness, onboarding and protected personnel tools
Choose the tools your business needs
Clockx provides the everyday staff-management essentials. Full Workspace adds wider people, document and cover workflows. Your business account determines the employee allowance and active tools.
Geo Clock-in works with both packages. Tasks and Stock Management require Full Workspace. Ask DayRidge to activate your chosen add-ons and confirm any Tasks chargeable-user allowance.
Your agreed package, employee allowance and enabled add-ons determine the account you use. A hidden menu can reflect the package or role rather than a fault.

title: Give each person the right view
intro: The Business Owner is the primary business manager account. It is distinct from the DayRidge platform administrator who manages the service.
blocks: Business settings, team oversight, payroll and access control
Owner-level access to wage and gross-pay reporting
Plan rotas, review requests and manage worked-time records
Team payroll and wage reporting stay with the owner
Published shifts and individually granted team tools
No private employee files, bank details or payroll
Own shifts, attendance, leave and personal information
Own records; extra tools depend on the package
Package: does the business have this tool?
Add-on: has DayRidge enabled the purchased extra?
Person: does this account have the role or permission needed?

A Manager who also works shifts may have a linked employee profile and a My shifts & pay switch. Management access and an employee shift record serve different purposes; an employee profile uses an employee place in the business allowance.
Give people the smallest set of permissions that lets them do their job. Revisit access when responsibilities change or someone leaves.

title: Invitations, passwords and access
intro: Start from the branded DayRidge app address and use an account connected to the correct business.
blocks: Open the invitation. Follow the account-setup email and complete the password flow. Use the email address your business has recorded for your account.
Sign in at the app. Open https://app.dayridge.co.uk/, enter your email address and password, and check the workspace name after signing in.
Use the right recovery route. If you have forgotten your password, use Forgot password? on the sign-in screen. Follow the latest valid recovery email.
Resend setup when needed. An authorised manager can use the account-setup resend control where shown for that person. Check spelling and junk folders before repeatedly requesting another email.
Escalate account state problems. If the business is paused, or the message says to contact the business manager, the owner should contact DayRidge about the business account.
Use your own account rather than sharing a Manager login.
Keep the manager kiosk PIN separate from employee PINs.
Sign out of private management views on shared devices.
Check your role and package first. Payroll and Business settings are owner-only. A Team Leader workspace is intentionally more focused than a Manager workspace.

title: Set the business up correctly
intro: These settings influence how the workspace identifies the business and how it presents budgets, pay periods and worked-time estimates.
blocks: Review business details. Enter the business name, trading name, address, business email and phone number. Save a suitable business logo if you want one shown across supported areas.
Choose pay frequency. Select Weekly, Fortnightly, Four-weekly or Monthly. For weekly pay, choose the payday weekday. For monthly pay, choose the day of the month.
Set an anchor where required. Fortnightly and four-weekly cycles need an anchor payday so future paydays can repeat on the intended cycle.
Check the preview. Review the next payday and pay-period dates before saving. Weekly cycles use the previous complete Monday-Sunday week; the monthly preview pays the previous calendar month.
Set the weekly labour budget. Use a positive amount that reflects your planning budget. Budget estimates support rota planning; they are not the final payroll total.
If a chosen monthly payday does not exist in a particular month, the app uses that month’s last day. A business logo must be PNG, JPG or WebP and no larger than 2 MB.
Automatic breaks are covered later in this guide. The annual leave year is managed by DayRidge administration: ask for the correct January-December or April-March policy to be configured.

title: Invite Managers and Team Leaders
intro: Create a clear management structure before handing over the working week. Access changes should match the responsibility you intend to delegate.
blocks: Choose the account type. The Business Owner can invite a full Manager. A Team Leader is a more limited account with focused permissions.
Enter the person’s name and email. Use an address they can access. Send the invitation and check that the management list reflects the expected account.
Set Team Leader permissions. The owner chooses extra access when inviting a Team Leader or uses Edit access afterwards. New extra permissions start off unless selected.
Review the actual experience. Ask the person to refresh their workspace and confirm that the expected sections appear.
Remove access when appropriate. Use the relevant Remove action after checking which account and role you are removing. Do not remove the wrong person simply because names are similar.
View team directory: active staff names and roles.
View open shifts and daily attendance totals, without wages.
Manage the team rota: draft shifts and individual publication.
Review annual leave: decisions and undoing upcoming approvals.
Team Leader permissions do not expose private employee files or payroll. Full Workspace personnel permissions and Stock permissions have their own controls.

title: Add and maintain employee records
intro: A reliable employee record connects rota planning, clocking, leave and payroll hours. Check the basics rather than rushing through account creation.
blocks: Enter the employee’s identity. Check their name, role and account email. Use the employee number assigned in the business and give them their personal clocking PIN through an appropriate private channel.
Set employment inputs carefully. Review start date, regular or irregular working pattern and contracted hours or days where required. These inputs affect leave estimates and other summaries.
Check owner-only pay information. The owner should verify the hourly rate used for estimates. Standard Managers and Team Leaders do not receive team wage reporting.
Decide whether onboarding is required. If you already hold the information, do not ask the employee to complete the same form unnecessarily. Use the option available in the creation flow.
Confirm setup. Check the new record appears, the invitation has reached the correct person and they can see their own workspace.

Adding a person beyond the approved employee allowance can require DayRidge approval. Use the account’s upgrade/request route rather than creating duplicate records. Archiving a leaver and deleting an unused setup record are different actions; read the confirmation before proceeding.
Check the employee number and PIN on the actual workplace device. Fix account mismatches before people start using each other’s records.

title: Onboard a new starter
intro: Onboarding gathers starter information for authorised review. It can be required or marked unnecessary when the business already has what it needs.
blocks: Explain what is needed. Tell the employee whether the onboarding form is required and where to find it. The form can contain identity, address, starter-tax and bank information.
Employee completes the form. They review the requested fields and submit it. A submitted form is awaiting review; submission alone is not owner approval.
Review the information. Use the Onboarding workspace to check the employee and the status. Confirm the information matches the person you intended to onboard.
Approve or request changes. Follow the available review controls. If something is incomplete, explain what needs correcting rather than approving an uncertain record.
Complete your business process. Make sure your approved personnel and payroll process has the information it needs. Do not treat the submitted form as a substitute for a maintained employee file.
Not required, Not started, Awaiting review, Approved and Changes requested describe different stages. Check the status after saving instead of assuming a form has been accepted.

title: Employee files and personal changes
intro: Keep personal information under the right access controls. An employee can propose changes to their own details; authorised people review the request.
blocks: Open the correct record. Use Employee files and identify the employee before reviewing contact, emergency or other personnel information.
Review incoming changes. Employees use My details to submit changes to supported contact and bank fields. Check the proposed values before approving a request.
Separate bank-related access. Review the permission controls carefully; bank information is more sensitive than a team directory entry.
Manage delegated access. The Business Owner controls which authorised Managers can access or approve protected personnel information. Give access only where their role requires it.
Review profile photos. Employee profile-photo submissions can await an authorised manager’s decision before appearing to the team.

Submitting a change does not mean the business has accepted it. Employees should check the status and tell the owner promptly about time-sensitive changes. A contact-information update does not automatically decide or complete a payroll change.
A team list is not a personnel file
The team directory is for operational names and roles. It should not be used to circulate private personal, bank or onboarding information.

title: Build the working week
intro: The rota is a plan for who should work and when. It is separate from the record of hours actually worked.
blocks: Choose the week. Use the week arrows or This week. Check the dates displayed above the board before adding shifts.
Add a shift. Use Add a shift or the plus control in a person’s day cell. Choose the employee, date, start and end times and role details shown in the form.
Work in draft. Draft shifts let you prepare the plan before employees see it. Check coverage, repeated entries and the correct people.
Review availability and leave. Approved leave appears on the board and blocks conflicting additions. Resolve a mismatch rather than forcing a shift onto an unavailable person.
Check the labour picture. The owner can review planned hours and estimated costs against the weekly budget. Open shifts can contribute to planning totals where that tool is available.
Publish when ready. Use the publishing control for the relevant week. Ask one employee to confirm the published shift appears in their personal view.
A saved draft is still a planning record. It does not give employees a published shift. Check the published status after saving and after editing.

title: Publish, correct and find cover
intro: Check the impact of a change before saving it. A clear process prevents the rota, employee expectations and actual attendance from drifting apart.
blocks: Editing a shift: open the shift chip and check the employee, date and times before saving. If you are changing an already communicated plan, tell the affected employee through your normal process.
Overlapping shifts: the app blocks clashes. Check whether the person already has another shift and whether the date or overnight end time is wrong.
Approved leave: do not work around a leave clash by creating a duplicate employee. Review the leave decision and intended dates first.
Removing a shift: read the confirmation and distinguish a planned rota shift from a completed worked-time entry. Removing a plan should not be treated as correcting a clocking record.
Sickness cover: supported Full Workspace rota controls can create an open cover offer for an eligible upcoming published shift. Review the absence and the dates first.
Check the result in both places
After a material change, review the manager rota and the employee’s published schedule. Use Activity to see recorded management changes and to help resolve questions.

title: Read the shift calendar
intro: The month calendar brings planned work, recorded shifts and time away into a clear date-based view. Select a date for the underlying detail.
where: Employee > My shifts / Rota > Month calendar
blocks: Choose whose calendar to view. In the Manager rota month view, select the team member. Employees see their own schedule.
Move between months. Use the left and right arrows. Today returns you to the current date. The month changes directly; it is not a native month-selection wheel.
Read the key. Green shows upcoming or completed shifts, orange overtime and purple time away such as approved holiday or recorded sickness. Split colours show more than one type on the same date.
Select a day. Read the listed times and status rather than drawing conclusions from the colour alone. A past scheduled shift is not proof that the employee actually clocked in.
Refresh when needed. Use the refresh control after a recent decision or correction. Check that the month and person still match the record you intended to review.
The calendar above illustrates the colour key. Your actual dates, shift totals and details come from the records and permissions in your workspace.

title: Open shifts and extra hours
intro: Use cover and overtime tools to handle changes to the working week without confusing requests with confirmed work.
blocks: Review the uncovered work. Check the date, role, times and current status of an open shift. Make sure the offer still reflects the cover you need.
Review employee requests. Eligible employees can request an open shift. A request is not a confirmed allocation until the appropriate decision is saved.
Check suitability and clashes. Review existing shifts, leave and availability before approving cover. Consider the full working week, including overnight work.
Record the decision. Use the available approve or decline action and check the updated status. Tell the employee about any material change to their expected shift.
Handle extra-hours requests. Review the requested date, times and reason in Requests. Approval records the decision; attendance still needs a clocking or authorised worked-time record.
An open shift is a staffing opportunity.
An approved request is a management decision.
A worked-time entry records the time actually completed.
Open shifts and extra-hours requests are Full Workspace tools. They are not part of the Clockx package.

title: Review holiday requests clearly
intro: Check the requested dates, the employee’s balance and the effect on cover before making a decision.
blocks: Open the pending request. Check the person, start date, end date and the estimated leave hours. Compare the request with the rota and existing leave.
Review the balance. Check start date, working pattern and contracted hours. Estimates depend on the employee inputs, recorded information and the configured leave year.
Approve or decline. Save the decision using the request controls and verify the new status. Approved leave reduces the available balance and blocks rota shifts on those dates.
Undo an upcoming approval when needed. Use the undo/cancellation action where available and read the confirmation. Check the request and balance again after it saves.
Resolve year-boundary requests. Split a request that crosses the leave-year boundary into the appropriate periods rather than assuming a single total belongs to one year.

The displayed entitlement is an estimate to review alongside your business’s agreed terms. If the balance is surprising, check the underlying employee record and dates first. Ask DayRidge to correct the configured leave year if it is wrong.
Full Workspace Team Leaders can review leave only if the owner grants that permission. Sickness is a separate record and does not deduct annual leave.

title: Record sickness and the return
intro: Keep absence dates accurate and separate from holiday approval. An expected return is a planning date; an actual return closes the absence record.
blocks: Record the absence. Identify the employee and first day absent. Enter the supported expected-return information if it is known.
Review ongoing records. Use the Ongoing filter to identify who is still off. An absence past the expected date needs follow-up; it should not be assumed to have ended.
Update dates when the position changes. Use Edit dates to correct the supported absence details. Keep the expected return realistic for planning purposes.
Mark the employee returned. When they return, use Mark returned and save the actual return date. Complete the return-to-work discussion and follow-up fields shown in that workflow.
Review date-only trends. Use the absence overview’s date range to see aggregate patterns. Check the selected period before comparing totals.

The sickness workspace is designed for restricted absence dates and return information. Do not enter diagnoses or other medical detail into operational notes. Sickness is recorded, not approved, and does not reduce annual leave.
If absence affects a future rota shift, review cover separately. Do not edit a sickness record merely to make a staffing total look correct.

title: Set up and use the kiosk
intro: The kiosk is the shared workplace clocking view. It uses employee numbers and personal PINs, with manager access protected by a separate kiosk PIN.
blocks: Choose the workplace device. Open the correct business workspace and enter the workplace kiosk through the supported manager control.
Complete device setup if requested. Use the manager setup flow for the workplace device. Confirm the business shown is the one whose staff will use it.
Keep manager access private. The manager kiosk PIN is six digits. Store and communicate it only to the people who should unlock or exit the protected kiosk.
Explain employee clocking. Employees enter their own employee number and personal PIN, then follow the clock-in or clock-out flow shown on the device.
Check a real result. After a pilot clocking, confirm the correct employee appears in the team clock status. At the end, confirm the completed record and break information.
Do not use one employee number for several staff.
Do not leave the owner’s private dashboard open on the shared kiosk.
If a clocking fails, check the number, PIN and device state before creating another employee.
Kiosk and personal clocking are different routes
Employees may also have My Time Clock in their signed-in account. Explain which route your business expects them to use.

title: Clock in, clock out and check
intro: Published shifts describe the plan. Successful clock-ins and clock-outs create the worked-time record used in attendance and payroll-hour summaries.
where: My Time Clock / Manager > Time clock
blocks: Employee starts work. Use the personal clocking page or workplace kiosk. Wait for the app to confirm the clock-in; an unsaved tap is not a recorded shift.
Employee checks the active shift. My Time Clock shows whether they are clocked in, the elapsed timer and a current earnings estimate where available.
Manager checks the team. Use the team clock status to review who is working. The manager’s own personal shift should use their linked employee profile.
Employee finishes work. Choose Clock out and complete the confirmation. Check the result rather than leaving the page during saving.

Resolve a missed clocking. An authorised Manager can clock an employee in or out and adjust the relevant time through supported manager controls. Record the actual agreed time, not a convenient default.

A clock-in already saved to DayRidge is not erased because the page closes or briefly becomes unavailable. When access returns, refresh and check the active record. A failed or unconfirmed new action still needs review.
The elapsed timer and earnings display are live estimates. Unpaid breaks and authorised corrections can change the final worked hours.

title: Set the workplace clock-in area
intro: Place the workplace accurately, check the allowed radius and save it before employees use location-checked clock-in.
blocks: Geo Clock-in is available with Clockx and Full Workspace after DayRidge activates the add-on. The Business Owner saves workplace settings; other Managers can view the saved map.
Open Choose on map. Open Geo Clock-in in Business profile. If a workplace is saved, the map shows its pin and allowed circle. Otherwise choose the actual premises before saving.
Place the purple pin. Drag the pin, tap the map or pan to the right position and choose Use map centre. You can also use Set location from this device while on site, then refine the position.
Check the allowed radius. Choose a whole number from 50 to 1,000 metres. A 100-metre radius is a starting point to check on site. Show allowed area fits the circle into view.
Save deliberately. Moving the pin or getting a device location changes the draft fields. Press Save workplace location to apply the coordinates and radius.
Review with the team. Tell employees how to allow precise location and confirm a first real clock-in at the workplace. Moving the workplace pin does not remove their phone location check.
If the map cannot load, close it and use current-device location or manually entered latitude and longitude. Check the workplace and save the form.

title: Help people clock in on site
intro: The location check applies to personal-phone clock-ins. A failed check does not start a shift, so employees should report a problem promptly.
where: Employee > My Time Clock / Business profile
blocks: Arrive and open My Time Clock. The employee chooses Clock in and allows the browser to obtain a fresh precise location.
Check the result. Confirm the running shift appears. DayRidge checks the distance and reported accuracy before accepting the clock-in.
Resolve a blocked permission. Allow location for app.dayridge.co.uk in the browser website settings, check the phone location setting, then refresh and try again.

On iPhone Safari, check both settings. In Safari’s Page Menu, allow Location for the website. In iPhone Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > Safari Websites, allow location while using the app and enable Precise Location.
Handle a weak or outside-area fix. Recheck the saved workplace pin, move to a safe place with a better signal and retry. Do not widen the area just to accept an unexplained remote location.
Use the business fallback. A registered workplace kiosk retains its device/PIN flow. A Manager can record an arrival override with a reason when needed. Clocking out does not need a location check.
There is no continuous tracking. These Geo functions do not retain raw employee coordinates. Browser locations may be inaccurate or spoofed, so a check is not a guarantee of physical presence.
Tell the Manager the business, the time, the message and the phone/browser used. A location error alone is not proof that someone is absent or late.

title: Break rules and time corrections
intro: Review recorded breaks and saved automatic rules together. The same break should not be deducted twice.
blocks: Configure new shifts: in Business, set whether automatic unpaid breaks are enabled, the shift length that must be exceeded and the unpaid minutes to apply.
Understand the saved rule: new clock-ins and manually added shifts use the current rule. Existing shifts keep the rule saved with them; changing today’s setting does not rewrite every old record.
Compare manual and automatic breaks: where a longer recorded break exists, that value is used. Review the displayed total unpaid break rather than adding the two deductions together.
Correct a completed shift: find the employee’s past shift, use Edit, review start, end and unpaid break, then save. Check overnight dates carefully.
Delete only an erroneous entry: read the confirmation and check the employee and dates. A genuine worked shift normally needs a correction rather than deletion.
The example shows 8 elapsed hours less a 30-minute unpaid break, giving 7.5 paid hours. Your business rule and the actual saved record determine the real result.

title: Prepare hours for payroll
intro: Use DayRidge to review recorded hours and gross estimates, then hand the checked information to your normal payroll process.
blocks: Check the pay schedule. Review the owner’s Business settings and the period being reported. A wrong anchor or monthly day can put otherwise correct shifts in the wrong view.
Review every employee. Check missing clock-outs, duplicate shifts, unexpected durations and unpaid breaks. Resolve the underlying attendance record before relying on a total.
Review hourly rates. Confirm the owner-only employee pay inputs are correct. A changed rate or correction can affect estimated gross amounts.
Use the supported export. Export the recorded attendance/payroll hours through the available CSV control and check the downloaded period and employee numbers.

Finish payroll in your established process. Apply the business’s approved payroll rules, deductions and final checks outside the worked-hours review. Keep an agreed copy of the export you actually used.
Gross earnings estimates are not take-home pay. DayRidge’s time and pay summaries do not calculate every tax, pension, statutory payment or adjustment, and they do not issue payslips.
Business payroll and team wage reporting belong to the Business Owner. Employees see their own information; standard Managers and Team Leaders do not receive team payroll access.

title: Share contracts and policies
intro: Choose the correct audience before sharing. A company document and a private employee contract are not the same kind of record.
blocks: Choose the document type. Prepare a private employee contract or upload a company document. Select the intended employee when using private scope.
Prepare the content. Use the contract editor or upload an existing supported file. Give it a clear title and description. Supported uploads include PDF, DOCX, PNG and JPG up to 10 MB.

Check the sharing choice. Leave Share now off to save a draft. Company documents shared with the business are visible to active members; private employee documents are limited to the selected employee and authorised management.
Choose acknowledgement. Decide whether staff must mark the document as read. A review date, or a certificate expiry date where that category is used, helps identify records that need attention.
Review receipts and lifecycle. Open the document to see recorded read receipts. Drafts can be edited or deleted. Shared documents can be archived or restored through supported controls.
A contract’s Acknowledge receipt action records that the employee received/read it. It does not sign the contract or accept its terms. Use your own approved signing process when one is needed.
Archived company documents leave the staff library. Employees retain access to their own previous contracts, and read receipts remain recorded.

title: Assign individual work
intro: Use individual tasks when a particular employee needs a clear action, instructions and deadline. Use shared shift checklists for a job that only needs doing once.
blocks: Confirm activation. Tasks is a paid add-on for Full Workspace. Ask DayRidge to enable it for the purchasing business and confirm the agreed chargeable-user count.
Create the task. Enter a concise title, useful instructions and a due date where needed. Explain what finished work should look like.
Assign the right people. Select the intended employee or employees. For individual assignments, each person’s progress is tracked separately.
Employee progresses the work. In My Tasks, they review instructions and move their own assignment through To do, In progress and Complete using the available controls.
Review the result. Use the manager view to check completion and overdue work. Follow up on missing work through the business’s normal management process.
A shared opening, closing or shift check
One task claimed by one person from eligible shifts
Structured answers and optional required live photos
Give tasks a clear owner and sensible due date. Avoid repeating a shared job as multiple individual assignments when the team only needs it completed once.

title: Build a reusable shift checklist
intro: A checklist template defines the job. Allocating it to published shifts creates a shared task for that working day.
blocks: Create the template. Give the checklist a title and instructions. Examples include opening checks, a handover or a close-down routine.
Add structured fields. Choose checkboxes, text answers, numbers or selection options. Mark the fields that are required and make question wording specific enough to answer consistently.
Choose evidence requirements. Enable Require photo evidence where the job genuinely benefits from a fresh photograph. Do not require unnecessary images of people or private information.
Allocate to the shift. Choose the saved template, the working date and the relevant published employee shifts. Publish the rota first if no shifts are available.
Check the shared run. The selected shift group shares a checklist that only needs completing once. The board shows Available, In progress or Completed, who took it and the relevant timestamps.
Completion is recorded, not a separate approval stage
Managers can inspect answers, evidence and completion details. Do not describe this as an appraisal, electronic signature or a separate manager sign-off workflow.

title: Take ownership and finish the job
intro: Employees can claim an available shared shift task, complete the required answers and capture fresh evidence in the app.
blocks: Choose active work. The active view shows new and in-progress work. Completed tasks are available in their separate view instead of sitting under the main list.
Take the task. Open an available checklist and choose Take task. Check that your name appears as the person who has taken it. Other colleagues can see that it is already owned.
Answer the checklist. Read the instructions and complete required fields. Use the right units for numeric answers and explain relevant exceptions in supported text fields.

Take live evidence where needed. Choose Take photo, allow camera access and capture the scene in the branded camera dialog. Gallery uploads are disabled in this workflow. Required-photo checklists need at least one live image.
Complete or release. Submit completion when the job is finished. If you cannot do it, use the supported release action to return the task to the board rather than leaving it claimed indefinitely.

A checklist can hold up to five photos. If the camera is blocked, review the browser’s camera permission for the DayRidge app and try again. Capture the task itself; a fresh photo does not replace a manager’s review of the actual work.
Inspect the recorded answers, claimant and time, and open evidence photos where needed. Use the Completed tasks area to find finished work.

title: Set up products and permissions
intro: Start with consistent product records. Accurate units and prices matter more than a long product list with inconsistent assumptions.
blocks: Confirm the add-on. Stock Management must be active for the business. The owner or authorised access manager controls which Managers can use it.
Create a product. Use Add product and enter a clear name, product code or category where relevant, counting unit, purchase cost and selling price.

Choose one usable unit. Count the same product in the same unit throughout opening counts, deliveries, waste and closing stock. Decide whether a unit means an item, bottle, measure or another supported unit.
Review prices. Keep purchase costs, selling prices and till figures on a consistent tax and pricing basis chosen by the business.
Check operational access. Give count-entry access to the appropriate Managers. Delegate access-management permission only where it is needed.

Write down any business-specific unit convention before the first stocktake. If stock is bought in one pack size but sold in another, decide and consistently apply the conversion you will enter. The app does not automatically turn recipes, portions or yields into stock units.
This version uses entered counts, movements and till amounts. Do not assume it is connected directly to your till or that it imports sales automatically.

title: Run a stocktake you can trust
intro: A useful stocktake compares physical counts and relevant movements over the same period as the till sales being reviewed.
blocks: Start the record. Choose New stocktake and give the period a recognisable title. Check opening and closing count times before entering figures.
Confirm the opening position. Enter the first opening count where needed or check the supported opening balance carried from the preceding record.
Record movements. Account for deliveries, waste, complimentary items and relevant adjustments using consistent product units. Give a reason when a correction or non-sale movement needs one.
Count closing stock. Enter what is physically present at the closing point. Recheck an unusually high or low quantity before relying on calculated usage.
Match the sales period. Enter the relevant till sales for exactly the same period and products. Avoid comparing a whole-day till total with a partial-shift count.
Save or complete. Save unfinished work as a draft, then reopen it when you can finish. Review the count and sales comparisons before completing the stocktake.
Keep stocktakes in a sensible chronological sequence. Later records can depend on an earlier closing count. Review dependencies before deleting or changing a linked record.

title: Explain stock and till differences
intro: Use differences to start a review of the underlying figures. A variance is a signal to investigate, not an automatic explanation of what happened.
blocks: Check the sign. Difference is recorded till sales minus expected sales. A negative amount is short; a positive amount is over.
Check the inputs first. Review count dates, units, deliveries, waste, complimentary items, adjustments and selling prices. Recount where appropriate.
Record an investigation note. Identify the product or whole stocktake, explain the discrepancy and keep an actionable follow-up. Use the supported open/resolved state.
Use analytics carefully. Choose the reporting period before comparing usage, sales or product performance. Make sure the included stocktakes are comparable.
Handle deleted records deliberately. Deleted stocktakes can be viewed and restored through Show deleted stocktakes. Later stocktakes that depend on the closing count must be dealt with first.
A short figure may come from a count, price, timing or entry issue. Check the evidence before deciding what action the business should take.

title: Use Activity and notifications
intro: A good review starts with the underlying record. Notifications help you notice work; Activity helps you understand recorded management changes.
blocks: Open Activity. Review the recorded actor, summary and time for changes such as rota publishing, timesheet edits, requests and settings.
Filter by category. Use All activity, Rota, Timesheets, Requests, Team or Settings to narrow the question you are investigating.
Open the relevant workspace. Compare the activity entry with the current shift, request or employee record. A historical event and a current status can both be correct.
Use the bell as an inbox. Read the notification and follow its link to the work that needs attention. Marking a notification as read does not approve the underlying request.
Confirm the actual outcome. Check the saved request status, published shift or corrected worked-time record after taking action.
Who published or amended the rota?
Did someone change the business settings?
Your business account does not include DayRidge’s provider finance console, website-traffic dashboard or management of other customers. Ask DayRidge about your subscription or service account.

title: A simple operating rhythm

intro: Start with the message on screen. Fix the actual account or device issue rather than creating duplicate staff or repeatedly retrying the same action.
where: Sign in / Managers / Team / My Tasks

title: Hours, balances and stock totals
intro: Unexpected totals usually need a review of inputs, dates and record status. Check those before making a correction.
blocks: Why is a shift total wrong?
Employee and date; clock-in/out; overnight end date; manual break; saved automatic-break rule; duplicate worked-time entries.
Why does the rota differ from hours?
A rota is a plan; attendance records what was saved as worked time. Review the actual clockings and any authorised corrections.
Why is an earnings estimate different?
Recorded hours, unpaid breaks, rate and pay period. Gross estimates exclude payroll deductions and are not net pay.
Why is the leave balance unexpected?
Employee start date, regular/irregular pattern, contracted hours, configured leave year, approved leave and the request dates.
An expected return date does not close the record. Check whether an actual return was saved through Mark returned.
Why can nobody take a checklist?
Check the allocated published shifts and whether a colleague has already claimed it. Use release when it needs returning to the board.
Why is stock showing a difference?
Opening/closing times and units; physical counts; movements; prices; till period and entered sales. Check like-for-like figures.
Refresh and check the source record, the affected total and any export you intend to use. Keep a note of the business reason where the workflow provides one.

title: One shift, from plan to payroll
intro: This fictional example connects the workflows. It is a way to check your setup, not a promise that every business uses the same rates or break policy.
blocks: Owner plans the week. Gabbie is scheduled from 09:00 to 17:00. The Manager checks coverage and publishes the shift. Gabbie can now see the plan in My shifts.
Gabbie records the day. A confirmed 09:00 clock-in starts the active attendance record. The rota alone would not have created a completed worked shift.
The team shares a job. With the Tasks add-on active, Gabbie takes an available closing-checklist task allocated to the published shift group. Colleagues can see that it has an owner.
Gabbie completes the checklist. Required answers and a live photo are submitted. The completed task moves into the separate completed-work area, with the claimant and completion time recorded.
Manager checks clock-out and breaks. A 17:00 clock-out gives eight elapsed hours. If the applicable total unpaid break is 30 minutes, paid hours are 7.5.
Owner reviews payroll hours. At a fictional £12.50 hourly rate, 7.5 hours gives £93.75 gross before payroll deductions. The owner checks the period and exports the reviewed hours.
Published rota, recorded attendance, task completion and payroll review are related records. None should be assumed to prove all the others.
